finding: ReadHeaderTimeout alone leaves ordinary HTTP body reads, writes and idle keepalive lifetime without explicit application limits; upgraded handshake writes also need their own timeout.
scope: Central production HTTP server configuration retains routes, address, diagnostics logger and five-second header deadline.
Add ten-second ordinary request-read/response-write and sixty-second idle-keepalive limits plus a16KiB configured MaxHeaderBytes value.
Set Gorilla's upgrade-handshake write timeout to five seconds; leave origin checks and disabled WebSocket compression unchanged.
After a successful upgrade Gorilla clears ordinary HTTP deadlines; the game's existing Pong and new fixed fragment-assembly deadlines govern that transport.

checks.productionConfiguration: Actual factory defaults, original address/routes/logger, handshake timeout and disabled compression asserted.
checks.actualOversizedHeaders: 32KiB probe header returns HTTP431 before application handler invocation under the configured production header limit.
checks.actualIdleExpiry: Ordinary keepalive response succeeds, then server closes the idle connection under a shortened100ms fixture deadline.
checks.actualIncompleteRequests: Incomplete header cannot reach a handler; a partial request body times out. Both use shortened100ms fixture deadlines.
checks.actualBlockedResponse: A disposable8MiB response to an unread, small-receive-buffer loopback peer releases its blocked writer with a network timeout under a shortened200ms fixture deadline.
checks.actualWebsocketUpgrade: Production upgrader retains a usable loopback WebSocket after150ms, beyond the fixture's50ms ordinary HTTP read/write/idle limits, with exact message echo.

limits: Shortened loopback timing exercises the actual HTTP implementation; it is not a minute-long default-idle test, production login, TLS renewal, database or proxy acceptance.
Go net/http may read bounded parser slack beyond configured MaxHeaderBytes. This is not an exact16KiB raw-wire accounting claim.
Handshake timeout value is asserted; the upgrade check proves HTTP-deadline clearance, not a malicious stalled handshake-write experiment.
No global ordinary HTTP connection/arrival cap or upstream denial-of-service protection is established by these deadlines.
Worker admission, jump policy, latest-source connected/load evidence and other roadmap gates remain open; milestone1.72 is not complete.
